Ancient DNA shows Ice Age humans targeted female mammoths

Ancient DNA recovered from mammoth remains across Eurasia and North America indicates that Ice Age hunters killed female mammoths far more often than males, a pattern researchers say points to deliberate selection rather than chance encounters on the open steppe.

The team analysed nuclear DNA from more than five hundred specimens, assigning sex to each and comparing the ratios found at butchery sites with those expected from natural mortality. The imbalance held across regions and millennia.

Because mammoth herds were matriarchal, targeting females would have been both easier and more disruptive to herd survival, which may help explain the pace of the species' decline as human populations expanded northward.
